requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:30-55: authorizes, trims the name, slugifies default/explicit slugs, scopes uniqueness to the entity and maps a race QueryException to ValidationException. app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:34-76: nullable named arguments, ignores the queue's own id in the unique rule, maps races, supports deactivation. app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:37-87: validates array/list and QueuePermission entries, rejects cross-entity memberships, upserts/revokes and audits granted/revoked (no revoke log when nothing was deleted). app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:23-77: create/update/manageAccess/call, with managers always allowed, employee grant lookup and corrupted non-array denial. app/Models/Ticket.php:105-113 and app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:43 enforce active -> authorize -> waiting order. Migration 2026_10_29_050658_create_queue_access_table.php:16-22, app/Models/QueueAccess.php:18-49, app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:8 and database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:28-33 satisfy the schema/model/enum/factory contract; docs and CHANGELOG are updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes are in app/Actions/* with authorization inside the action (CreateQueue.php:30, UpdateQueue.php:34, SetQueueAccess.php:37). The migration is generator-style with a reversible down() (migration:29-32). QueueAccess uses #[Fillable] deliberately (QueueAccess.php:19). Tests use factories and the shared memberOf helper (tests/Pest.php:59-67). Audit logging uses Log::channel('audit') (SetQueueAccess.php:59,83). docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md are kept in sync.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes before writing (CreateQueue.php:30, UpdateQueue.php:34, SetQueueAccess.php:37); both call paths use Gate::forUser(...)->authorize('call', ...) (CallNextTicket.php:43, Ticket.php:109). All inputs are validated (CreateQueue.php:35-38, UpdateQueue.php:50-59, SetQueueAccess.php:39-42), QueueAccess mass assignment is limited via #[Fillable] (QueueAccess.php:19), and QueuePolicy denies grants whose stored permissions are not an array or omit call (QueuePolicy.php:67-68). No output rendering is touched by this slice.

tests.evidence: New Pest suites cover the slice: tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:13-125 (create, slug, duplicate, DB race, blank/length, authorization), UpdateQueueTest.php:19-169 (partial updates, re-slug, own/foreign slug, race, deactivation, authorization), SetQueueAccessTest.php:29-170 (grant/upsert/revoke, audit context, no-op revoke, unknown/non-string permissions, cross-entity, self-grant and outsiders), QueuePolicyTest.php:15-112 (all abilities, wrong queue, missing call, corrupted permissions), QueueAccessSchemaTest.php:13-66 (columns/index/cascade/cast/factory), and CallAuthorizationTest.php:37-152 (both call paths, every call mode, check ordering). Existing CallNextTicketTest was updated to use an authorized admin.

simplicity.evidence: The actions are small and delegate to Eloquent, Validator and Str, and the unique-violation check is reused through App\Support\UniqueViolation. However, the same QueryException-to-slug ValidationException block is duplicated in CreateQueue.php:46-55 and UpdateQueue.php:65-76.

readability.evidence: Focused methods with clear names and docblocks on each public action (CreateQueue.php:19-29, UpdateQueue.php:18-26, SetQueueAccess.php:19-30, QueuePolicy.php:20-49). No dead code, debug output or inconsistent formatting found.

scope.evidence: Almost everything in the diff serves the queue task (actions, policy, model/factory/migration, both call paths, tests, docs). The exception is app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:57-59, which refactors the existing unique-violation check into the new helper and drops its SQLSTATE 23000 fallback even though IssueTicket is not part of the queue requirements.

issues.explanation: Extracting the helper also drops IssueTicket's previous SQLSTATE 23000 fallback, so non-unique integrity errors are no longer retried; this is an unrequested behavior change to a file outside the queue task.
Both queue actions copy the same QueryException-to-slug ValidationException mapping; it could live beside UniqueViolation so the race handling exists in one place.

Both race tests call Queue::flushEventListeners() in a finally block, which removes every listener registered on the Queue model for the rest of the process; removing only the temporary closure (or using withoutEvents) avoids order-dependent failures.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle, per-queue grants, the QueuePolicy, both call-path checks, the schema/model/factory and the required docs and tests, with careful handling of races and corrupted permissions. I would approve after minor cleanup: the duplicated unique-violation mapping, the broad Queue::flushEventListeners() cleanup in the race tests, and the unrequested IssueTicket error-handling refactor.
